holidays.name: National Guacamole Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to celebrating the creamy, chunky, lime-spiked avocado dip that has launched a thousand chip-dipping sessions and at least as many office potluck arguments about whether peas belong in it (they do not).
holidays.origin: Celebrated in the United States on September 16, which coincides with Mexican Independence Day. The date ties the dip to its Mexican roots, as guacamole traces back to the Aztecs, who made it from mashed avocados.
holidays.funFact: The word guacamole comes from the Nahuatl word ahuacamolli, which literally means 'avocado sauce.' Some say the Aztecs also thought avocados were an aphrodisiac.

holidays.name: Mexican Independence Day
holidays.description: A huge national celebration in Mexico featuring fireworks, parades, mariachi music, and the famous 'Grito de Dolores' shouted from balconies and plazas, followed by lots of pozole and tequila.
holidays.origin: On September 16, 1810, priest Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla rang the church bell in the town of Dolores and called on citizens to rise up against Spanish colonial rule, starting the Mexican War of Independence.
holidays.funFact: Every year the Mexican president rings the very same bell from the Dolores church, which was moved to the National Palace in Mexico City, while delivering the Grito.

holidays.name: International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the invisible shield high above us that stops us from becoming crispy snacks for the sun, and to celebrate one of the rare times the whole world actually agreed on something.
holidays.origin: Designated by the United Nations in 1994 to commemorate the signing of the Montreal Protocol on September 16, 1987, which phased out substances that deplete the ozone layer.
holidays.funFact: The Montreal Protocol is often called the most successful environmental treaty in history, and scientists predict the ozone layer could return to 1980s levels by around the middle of this century.

holidays.name: Collect Rocks Day
holidays.description: A day when grown adults are encouraged to wander around with their eyes glued to the ground, pockets slowly filling with pebbles, because that one shiny stone is clearly special.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance created for hobbyists, geologists, and kids alike to celebrate the simple joy of collecting rocks, minerals, and stones.
holidays.funFact: Rock collecting is so popular that the hobby has its own name, rockhounding, and some people have collected rocks that turned out to be meteorites worth thousands of dollars.

holidays.name: Step Into Respect Day (Play Dough Anniversary Vibes)
holidays.description: A day to recognize that squishing, rolling, and sculpting colorful dough is a legitimate form of stress relief, and to honor everyone who has ever tasted it out of curiosity.
holidays.origin: Play-Doh fans often mark mid-September in tribute to the squishy compound, which began life in the 1930s as a wallpaper cleaner before being rebranded as a children's toy in the 1950s.
holidays.funFact: Play-Doh was originally sold as a putty to clean coal soot from wallpaper, and only became a toy after teachers noticed kids loved playing with it.
